# Digitone II: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-08, research snapshot `2e69cfba110a`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Brief version: rules, recovery, bugs, incidents and open questions. The full pack [digitone-2.md](digitone-2.md) adds all facts.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitone II

- **C5** (C) Windows: the DN2 tooling needs an m68k objdump; use WSL. `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}
- **C7** (C) Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying. Diff decoded content, check bootstrap and updater separately, re-find every patch by masked pattern (`find`/`expect`) and pin the build by hash; inspect unfamiliar sections first. (Digitone II 1.11 vs 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes.) `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions} {dn2-cfw-release-history}
- **C8** (C) Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines).
- **C9** (C) After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]`
- **C12** (C) Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes}
- **D6** (D) Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}
- **E2** (E) Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own. On the Digitone II (1.11) an edit is written into the stored sound record at once, so unsaved edits survive a power cycle; the writer is `Sound::updateMirror` (`0x4004ca80`). dnfw's LFO4 values did not survive until its setter sent the stock whole-sound event (`SoundConfigChangedInfo`) through the sound's holder; `updateMirror` then re-serialised the sound with LFO4's lane. Confirmed on the unit: unsaved LFO4 edits survive a power cycle, and SAVE PROJECT stores them. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}
- **E3** (E) Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}
- **E5** (E) Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot).
- **F5** (F) Never run parsers across device generations (Digitone mk1 device ID 0x0D vs Digitone II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2). `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}
- **G9** (G) DSP rules the emulators cannot check (Digitone II, each reportedly silenced or crashed a real unit): whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock instruction encodings only (incl. sign bits of negative shift immediates), PRM loop/DAG/branch rules, no L2 above `0x200B0000`, never read unwritten DDR (power-on NaN), preserve registers at hooks (clobbered R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio), count memory accesses not instructions. Details and addresses in [`devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md). `[hw]` {dn2-skill-sharc} Incidents: [I8](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I25](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i25-clobbering-r8-at-the-fx-bus-mixer-hook-lost-all-audio), [I26](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i26-a-boot-block-of-8n4-bytes-left-the-unit-silent), [I27](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip).

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [hw] Reported 2026-09-11: Transfer showed 100 % sent while the device bar froze near 80 %; stock 1.10E stalled over the same route, so the link was at fault, not the image. Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#719a2a9e`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L18))
- [hw] Fixes: prove the link with the stock firmware first; use a dedicated class-compliant USB-MIDI cable for long recovery transfers; disable Windows USB selective suspend and device power management; retry. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} (`flash-procedure#33d3b934`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L19))
- [hw] Proven on hardware: stock 1.10E via recovery (2026-09-08), stock 1.11 via recovery over a fixed link (2026-09-11); modified images via the normal update path. dnfw records no modified image completing the recovery route - recovery has been proven with stock only. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#eeccb444`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L20))
- [hw] A mod can break the normal USB update path without anyone noticing until the next update. On Overtone 1.0 (Digitone II), an OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing. The only way off it was the STARTUP menu over DIN, about 15 minutes. Test "install the next build over USB" as part of every release (rule A36). `[hw]` {overtone} ([I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path)) (`recovery#aa79ffc2`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L19))
- [doc] MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#f6ed5a32`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:14](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L14))
- [doc] Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} (`flash-procedure#243fba81`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L15))
- [doc] Back up with the `.dnx` backup before flashing; run `dnfw inspect` on the exact file you will send (build and patch only refuse output that does not verify). (`flash-procedure#386baed4`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L38))
- [doc] Keep the unmodified `.syx` in a firmware folder and never overwrite it with build output. (`flash-procedure#c54e3b5a`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L39))
- [doc] Change one thing per flash. (`flash-procedure#0debb1db`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L40))
- [doc] Do not patch the key material. (`flash-procedure#03c1c7d5`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:41](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L41))
- [doc] Do not start a flash on a crashing host (a previous workstation's `0x9F` crashes were tied to an NVIDIA driver). (`flash-procedure#0a1b43bb`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L42))
- [doc] The log records what was sent, not what is resident: write a row when stock goes back on. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#55e888f0`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:43](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L43))
- [doc] Two upgrade paths: from within the OS (Transfer, DROP page, confirm with YES on the device; devices whose OS does not fully support Transfer are sent to the LEGACY OS UPGRADE page) and from the Startup Menu (device's MIDI port, not USB; hold FUNC while powering on; TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; Transfer in LEGACY OS UPGRADE mode). `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#67684a45`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L28))
- [doc] "Some upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap" right after the first restart; do not turn the power off then. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#065677fb`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L29))
- [doc] Downgrading is not supported and is at the user's own risk; user content may be lost. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#258d6d79`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L30))
- [doc] Digitakt II, first reboot after upgrading to OS 1.15: a file-system integrity check (up to a minute). On errors: back up all projects and samples with Transfer, SETTINGS > SYSTEM > FORMAT +DRIVE (tick SAMPLES), re-import. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} (`recovery#00f8aff4`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L31))
- [doc] Heat +FX: in-OS path is SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with the file sent through MIDI In or USB MIDI In; the startup path takes MIDI In only. `[doc]` {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#2a7bab5e`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L32))
- [doc] Digitone II: same procedure; project slot 001 overwritten, loaded project cleared, sound banks A and B overwritten; other slots/banks untouched. ## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB1** eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry (TRIM is idempotent); fixed in dn2mk2 v0.40.
- **SB2** Song LOAD trusts a stored row count and halts the unit (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by the `songguard` mod (dn2_firmware_explore, also in dn2mk2): a damaged song loads empty; confirmed on hardware. Users: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`).
- **SB3** The USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: keep the container under 2 MiB; check the size in the build.
- **SB4** Auto-commit upload loses its "upload complete" event (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.
- **SB5** LFO TRIG MODE ONE and HALF do not run one (half) cycle and hold (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by the `lfolength` mod (dn2_firmware_explore; supersedes `lfohold`); confirmed on hardware on an audio track (2026-10-09), MIDI tracks in the emulator.

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I1** Stock eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card. Cause: after CMD38 the stock busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0; a short TRIM that finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post, so the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout. Fix: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry five times; ERASE PAUSED and resume on request (v0.40). Rules: A47.
- **I2** Stock song LOAD trusts a stored row count. Cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` copies `count` stored rows without checking it; the project held 21,503 rows instead of at most 99. Fix: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`, storage version 4); mods must keep every count in range. Rules: E3.
- **I3** USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit. Cause: the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the receiver does not check the size. Fix: keep the container under `0x200000` bytes. Rules: A30,A9.
- **I4** Auto-commit upload loses its "complete" event on the first upload after boot. Cause: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" while the upgrade view is not open yet; the event is lost. Fix: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself. Rules: A21.
- **I8** Power-on DDR holds garbage (often a NaN). Cause: DSP DDR is not cleared at power-on; the emulator zero-fills it and hides this. Fix: never read memory you did not write; fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests. Rules: G8,G9.
- **I9** A second application on the port corrupts SysEx replies. Cause: two clients share the USB MIDI port. Fix: close Transfer, Overbridge and DNX before a client run; check reply lengths. Rules: F7.
- **I70** A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller. Cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause. Fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes. Rules: A39.
- **I10** Byte-wise reads of uncached DMA buffers stalled the sequencer. Cause: the main OS sets CACR `0xa50ce100` / ACR0 `0x4007e020` (`0x40000000-0x47ffffff` cached); the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100` are uncached, and UM01 packed their slots with byte-wise reads. A first look at the bootstrap's CACR (cache off) gave a wrong conclusion. Fix: read each of the 14 SSI slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02): no lag with busy sequences. Rules: A48.
- **I12** A sample-machine mod could not create the storage it needed. Cause: R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one; stock FORMAT +DRIVE and the resets do not create it. Fix: R013 adds SYSTEM > FORMAT SAMPLES; formatting, Transfer capacity (~20 GB) and uploads passed on the unit. Rules: A49.
- **I13** USB audio repeated old audio after a project change. Cause: the TX selector follows RX completion and is no ownership grant; the build bound its queue head to a destination from an older phase. Fix: R011 picks the candidate from the current DMA START. Rules: C9.
- **I19** Patching a "free" zero run crashed the unit. Cause: the run was an array that the code fills at run time. Fix: two static checks (equal-stride gaps, referenced operands); only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both. Rules: D11,A43.
- **I21** MD and Monomachine tracks went silent after an install. Cause: unknown (suspected stale voice-slot state or state from an older version's project). Fix: none yet; test an old project after every install. Rules: C9.
- **I22** A mod broke the normal USB update path. Cause: the mod's build; fixed in 1.0.1. Fix: the STARTUP menu over DIN (~15 min); a release test that installs the next build over USB. Rules: A36,C9.
- **I25** Clobbering R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio. Cause: the mixer takes R4 and R8 as arguments; the hook changed R8. Fix: preserve every register and flag that code after a hook reads; compare callee registers between stock and the build. Rules: G9.
- **I26** A boot block of 8n+4 bytes left the unit silent. Cause: the L2 instruction-cache line fill over the block's end faults on ECC. Fix: whole 32-byte boot blocks (`dspblocks.pad_lines`, `bootblocks.py`). Rules: G9.
- **I27** An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip. Cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR). Fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly. Rules: A41,G9.
- **I51** The sample popup did not open after switching Machines. Cause: the separate sampler SYN view was not selected when the Machine changed within the audio-track class. Generic notifications redrew the old stock view. Earlier tests manually reselected SYN and hid the missing lifecycle transition. No live capture established that every intermittent popup report shares this cause. Fix: R021 defers reconciliation to the existing UI poll, uses native selection and ownership, and avoids modal/selected-trig transitions; included in R022. Rules: C8.
- **I52** New project samples were missing after reboot. Cause: load notification ran the native incremental settings serializer, but the port updated its sample companion only during whole-project serialization. Both prepared working backup and fresh emulated boot retained an empty identity for the loaded slot. The frozen device's actual backup state was not captured. Fix: R022 refreshes the working sample companion in that settings worker under the existing project lock, validates owner/UID, and preserves explicit saved checkpoints. Rules: E5.
- **I65** A machine kind past the end of a label table froze Digitone II units. Cause: the label lookup picked the Monomachine label table by range; BOUNCE (kind 13) read past its end and walked address `0xEE` as a list. The emulator reads low memory as zeros, which hid it (I66 has the gate side). Fix: one explicit test per machine kind, a `machines` gate step, and a trap on any non-stock read below `0x40000000` in every emulator step (v0.45). Recovery used: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 2 (EMPTY RESET; the +Drive is kept), then flash v0.45. Rules: A53.
- **I68** Spring-reverb builds lost their sound on a Digitone II; no cause found offline. Cause: not found. An offline search ruled out illegal instructions and accesses, parity, FP exceptions, the stack, Elektron's code, timing in digikit's coupled emulator, and digikit's SHARC+ silicon rules (checked on every build, no hit). The one lead: the spring's output is exactly 0 from 1.4 s into FX kill and 78 s after a stop, as at both unit stops [inferred]. Fix: the spring is shelved; its six builds stay withdrawn. The author stopped blind device tests. The next test build (EEEM, a light morphing reverb in the reverb slot) sends the stock DSP's idle parks to a fault tone whose pitch names the fault (1500 Hz illegal instruction, 3000 Hz parity, 6000 Hz emulation or default handler, 1500 + 6000 Hz abort or stack check; a ~750 Hz buzz or silence is a hang). Rules: A16.
- **I71** A DSP load guard dropped a sample voice block after block. Cause: the frame-time guard left the sample voice out when a block ran short of time, and because a sample voice is retried in every block it came and went block by block instead of stopping. Fix: planned for v0.49: render the sample voices first, so time runs out on the heavy synth voices, and keep a dropped sample voice stopped until its next note, as PERC voices already are. Rules: A44.
- **I37** A SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply. Cause: the emulator shifted every fractional multiply left; the PRM shifts only signed x signed. Fix: fixed in the emulator; `sharc_checks.py` calls stock routines and compares. Rules: C10.
- **I39** The default compression level corrupted a DN2 image. Cause: section 4's in-place loader has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's `-l 3` gives -39,318. Stock DT2 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). Fix: check the margin at every loader stage; a dense packer. Rules: A14.
- **I42** Checks reported success about work they never did. Cause: snapshot harnesses cleared code no real boot ran; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after its coverage section was deleted; an emulator call returned 0 for a present value. Fix: every check gets a control that must fail. Rules: C8.
- **I66** A feature that crosses ColdFire and DSP passed the gate and failed on units. Cause: unknown. The gate never ran the ColdFire and the DSP together. Per the v0.48 notes the recorder trigs fired and takes were made, but the track never played its buffer. Fix: BOUNCE removed from the menu in v0.47 and its code removed in v0.48 (old projects load, the track silent). v0.48 adds a coupled emulator that runs both processors one audio block at a time (faithful in order and content, not in timing margins) and the first gate step on it; FLEX, the replacement, is to be tested from recording to playback on it. Rules: C4,C2.
- **I43** Recovery stalled at ~80 %: the MIDI link, not the image. Cause: a USB MIDI interface went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets. Fix: a MIDI interface that stays awake for the ~12-15 min transfer. Rules: A11,A20.
- **I47** Stock storage resets did not create the sample filesystem. Cause: stock has no such filesystem on the DN2. Fix: the mod's own FORMAT SAMPLES (R013). Rules: A3,A49.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O20** DT2/DN2 stock intro frame rate: A) 30 Hz: digikit's PIT3 model (PCSR `0x093f`, PMR 8593), so the first scene table's 175 frames last 5.8 s (finding 117) B) 15 Hz: digikit's earlier emulator notes derive it from divisor 1024 (66.67 ms per frame; finding 07)
- **O19** DN2 SHARC L2 between `0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000`: A) in use: stock data words point to `0x200918c0`, `0x200c0008` and `0x200c1f84` (dnfw), so Digiwerk keeps new data out of the whole range and lists `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` as candidates B) usable: the DN2 modding skill places boot blocks at `0x20090000` (code) and `0x20098000` (data), hardware-proven, and sets the ceiling at `0x200b0000`; elekloader's master-output mod (`0x20090000-0x20098000`) ran on a unit for ten minutes, and its machines take `0x20090000-0x200b0000`
- **O16** What section 8 is for: A) the Outbox 8 accessory (dnfw: the image arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support; an inference from timing) B) the panel MCU firmware (analog-emu)
- **O6** DN2 1.11 parameter table base: A) `0x401f7fc8` (skill's map) B) `0x401f7fc4` (dnfw memory map)
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O9** Bootstrap write protection: A) DYB lock on sector `0x40000` (Spansion S25FL command) B) the DN2 board photographed carries a Winbond W25Q128JV, on which that lock does nothing
- **O12** DN2 load model: A) Digiwerk: load = (1.30 x instructions + 11k) / 666,667, predicted ~74 % B) the unit showed ~50-60 %
- **O13** Free top of the SHARC L1 blocks (DN2): A) static: L1 block 3 tail and block 1/2 tails are free (Digiwerk T3.2) B) the startup enables the caches there, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache
- **O15** DN2 stock DSP load at idle: A) ~63-65 % flat whatever plays (dnfw / Digiwerk idle-task method) B) ~80 % outside the idle task with nothing playing, falling to 65 % with 64 notes (elekloader dspbusy, 1,024-block windows)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H18** (stock) The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod. Test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.
- **H19** (stock) The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20). Test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).
- **H23** (stock) The ~4 KB cut in long MidiRpc LIST replies is in the stock reply router, not in a mod: an unpaged listing of a 256-entry table store on a modded DN2 came back as 3,997 bytes, correct up to entry 125 and garbage after; pages of 64 were clean. Test: On stock, list a +Drive folder with more than 130 entries in one unpaged request (DNX or Elektroid) and compare the reply length and the tail with a paged listing. Until settled, page listings at 64 entries or fewer.
- **H24** (stock) The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too. Test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.
- **H8** (probe) The DN2's digikit flash cave `0x402fb7a8` (2,136 B on 1.11) keeps its bytes through a cold boot, as the DT2's `0x403117c4` does. Test: A canary in the cave, read back after a cold boot and after playback. Combine with H9.
- **H10** (probe) DN2 L2 `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is not written by stock in normal use (O19). Test: A canary or a write watch over the range during playback, pattern changes and a save (T24).
- **H11** (probe) DN2 RAM `0x46700000-0x46701300` is written by stock only when a +Drive transfer is over 60,672 bytes (S17: project save and load reach it). Test: A canary at `0x46700000`, read back after loading a large sample or project from +Drive.
- **H12** (probe) Direct hook writes may race reply publication on a DN2. Digikit measured 3,995 of 4,000 zero diagnostic words on a DT2; its own diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's record in the DN2 emulator. Silicon DMA timing remains unmeasured. Test: Compare a hook's direct counter writes with static-word publication at block tail, without clearing prior reply records; count arrivals on the ColdFire side.
- **H13** (build) SIMD loads or stores into L2 byte space hang the DN2's DSP as they hang the DT2's (same core, same IMASK). Test: A one-variable probe image with one SIMD L2 access behind a key press; recovery by power cycle.
- **H15** (build) On the DN2, a single late DSP block is a one-block dropout that recovers, as on the DT2; the "silence until power cycle" reports came from sustained overload. Test: Provoke single late blocks (a burn loop on a key press) and count them on the DSP side; then hold an overload for seconds.
- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T8** (needs files, effort M) Build an address-translation table DN2 1.11 <-> 1.12 from shared anchors
- **T9** (needs unit, effort M) Measure DN2 load with both meters (dnfw idle-task and elekloader dspbusy) in the same states, then calibrate a cost model (dn2mk2's instructions + 4 x L2 + 10 x DDR is a start)
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)
- **T13** (needs PDF, effort S) Transcribe the official MIDI CC/NRPN tables from the manuals' appendices into `hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md`
- **T14** (needs unit + emulator, effort M) Fix or document digikit's EMAC fractional-mode emulation against a unit measurement
- **T16** (needs unit, effort S) Save a project on a grown parameter table, load it on stock, record what happens
- **T18** (needs files, effort M) Document the project file formats (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`) beyond song slots
- **T23** (needs reading, then unit, effort S) Keep a DN2 RAM tenancy table: every mod platform's and mod's ranges above the reset clear, per OS version (start: [memory-maps.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md), five projects compared 2026-11-02); then a unit canary at `0x46700000` after a large +Drive sample load (confirms S17, which dnfw settled from LFO4 project corruption)
- **T24** (needs emulator, then unit, effort S) Watch DN2 SHARC L2 `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` for stock writes during playback, pattern changes and a save (emulator write watch first, then a canary on a unit); settles O19

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

## 8. Mods, firmware, loaders and emulators for this device

- **digikit** (emulator, wip, tested: partly, base OS Digitakt II target 1.17 (emulator also runs 1.16 as default file; 1.15C kept for old analysis); Digitone II target 1.12 (also runs 1.11 as default file; 1.10E kept for old analysis)) https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit
- **Elektron Emu** (emulator, wip, tested: not stated, base OS one OS version per machine (named in each plug-in's README); not read by us) https://github.com/xerydian/elektron-emu
- **Elektron Emu (joshklomp)** (emulator, wip, tested: not stated, base OS user-supplied OS files) https://github.com/joshklomp/emu-elektron
- **DN2 DT2 firmware research** (firmware, stable, tested: not-stated, base OS Digitone II OS 1.11 (target) + Digitakt II OS 1.16 (donor); both official files supplied locally) https://github.com/armio/dn2-dt2-firmware-research
- **elekloader** (loader, active, tested: unit, base OS Digitakt mk1 1.53/1.54; Digitone mk1 + Keys 1.43/1.44; Digitakt II 1.17 (experimental); Digitone II 1.12 (experimental); Octatrack MKI/MKII 1.40C; Model:Cycles/Samples 1.13; Analog Rytm MKII 1.74; Analog Four MKII 1.56 (proof of concept). Analog Heat: not listed) https://github.com/elekloader/elekloader
- **DigiRust** (mod, beta, tested: not-stated, base OS Digitone II OS 1.12 (internal version stays 1.12)) https://github.com/nzimas/digirust
- **digitone-2-mod-hack** (mod, wip, tested: not-stated, base OS Digitone II) https://github.com/simonjohansson/digitone-2-mod-hack
- **DN2 mk2 Mod (dn2mk2-firmware)** (mod, wip, tested: emulator, base OS Digitone II stock OS 1.11 ONLY (1.10 must update to 1.11 first; 1.12+ must go back to 1.11). Also needs the user's own Digitakt II OS 1.17 (or 1.16), Machinedrum UW OS 1.63 and Monomachine SFX-6 OS 1.32B files) https://github.com/De-Pattern/dn2mk2-firmware
- **macro-mode (digi_macro)** (mod, wip, tested: partly, base OS Digitakt II OS 1.17 or Digitone II OS 1.12, exactly (the build checks the file's checksum)) https://github.com/toonst/digi_macro
- **Overtone** (mod, released, tested: unit, base OS Digitone II OS 1.12 only (patcher refuses any other file); NOT compatible with dn2mk2 (OS 1.11)) https://github.com/complex-ping/overtone
- **x0x (808/909 kick machines)** (mod, wip, tested: not-stated, base OS Digitakt mk1 1.54; Digitone mk1 1.44; Digitone II 1.12 (Digitakt II not supported)) https://github.com/simonjohansson/x0x
